summary: Yonten Gyatso was a Tibetology and history scholar. He earned a Geshé degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and a Diplôme at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he served as a research advisor for Tibetan Studies.

Yoshifumi Honjo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University, learning under Hajime Sakurabe. He held academic posts at Kobe Women's University, Bukkyo University, and Otani University, where he was professor from circa 2002 to 2017.

Yoshihide Yoshizu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his doctorate in Buddhist studies at Komazawa University, where he also taught as a lecturer and served as professor from circa 1989 to 2014.
Yoshihiko Nasu is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 2007). He has held leadership positions at Kongoju and Kongojushinkai.

Yoshihiko Sakurai is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed doctoral coursework at Ryukoku University and later served there as a part-time lecturer, as well as a researcher at Kyogaku Dendo Kenkyu Senta (both attested 2003).
Yoshitoyo Ohara is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyoto University (attested 2006) and the Kyoto National Museum (attested 2016).

Yoshihito Muroji is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He has held positions at Kyoto University, Koyasan University, and Shiga University of Medical Science.

Yoshiko Shimabukuro was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her studies at Kyoto Chuo Bukkyo Gakuen through 1936 and subsequently studied at Kyoto Women's University from 1936 to 1940.

Yoshinobu Kimoto is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He served as an assistant professor at Yonezawa Women's Junior College from circa 1987 to 1993 and held a post at Koshien Junior College around 1998.

Yoshinori Takeuchi was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1933 to 1936 and served as a professor there from circa 1959 to 1976.

Yoshio Kawakatsu was a Sinology and history scholar. He studied at Kyoto University, later studied under Paul Demiéville from circa 1956 to 1958, and held a post at Kyoto University from circa 1958 to 1984.

Yoshiro Imaeda is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Otani University and the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Ariane Macdonald and Bernard Frank, and served as a researcher at the CNRS from circa 1974 to 2012.

Yoshiro Tamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Toyo University, the University of Tokyo (chair in Japanese Buddhism, ~1972–1982), Rissho University, and the University of Chicago (1985).

Yoshitaka Iriya was a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He headed Nagoya University's Chinese Literature Department (~1957–1968) and held professorial posts at Kyoto University, Kyoto Sangyo University, and Hanazono University.

Yoshitsugu Sawai is a religious studies and Indology scholar. He earned doctorates from Tohoku University and Harvard University, studying under John B. Carman and Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and served as a professor and dean at Tenri University (~1993–2017).
Yoshiyasu Yonezawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held appointments as a researcher (attested 1998–2006) and as a specially appointed lecturer (attested 2015) at Taisho University.
Yoshiyuki Kawazoe studied at Tohoku University from circa 1966 to 1975. He subsequently held an academic post at Tohoku University from circa 1975 to 2012.
Yosho Nomura was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University from circa 1935 to 1939 and later served there as a professor from circa 1961 to 1987 and as director in the 1980s.

Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean, and later taught at Rowan University and The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Yozo Taniyama is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He held academic posts at St. Thomas University, Japan, Shitennoji University, Sophia University, and Tohoku University's Department of Practical Religious Studies.
